title: Governance and control environment: oversight, competence, and accountability for security
Communication of security responsibilities and of the information needed to meet them
Risk assessment: objectives, identification of risks to them, and consideration of change
Monitoring: evaluating whether controls operate, and remediating what does not
Selection and deployment of control activities, including through technology and policy
Logical and physical access: identity, authorisation, credentials, transmission, and disposal
notes: The broadest series, and the one a derived security baseline reaches most completely.

title: System operations: detecting anomalies, responding to incidents, and recovering
Change management: authorising, designing, testing, and deploying changes
Risk mitigation for business disruption and for vendors and business partners
Availability: capacity, environmental protection, and recovery to meet commitments
Processing integrity: processing that is complete, valid, accurate, timely, and authorised
notes: The category a security baseline reaches least well: correctness of business processing is not what a control catalogue is about.

title: Confidentiality: identifying confidential information and disposing of it when no longer needed
Privacy: notice, choice, collection, use, retention, disposal, access, disclosure, and quality
notes: Assessed against the AICPA privacy criteria, which are not the GDPR articles; where both apply, run both overlays.
